payload.request: Complete Swift 6 strict concurrency compliance for OpenOats codebase (~1400 errors). Fix actor-protocol conformance, Sendable violations, async-safe locking, and visibility issues. Enable full test suite compilation and CI/CD pipeline.
goals: Achieve zero Swift 6 strict concurrency errors
Enable full test suite compilation (OpenOatsTests target)
Document all @unchecked Sendable with safety rationale
Enable CI/CD pipeline for automated testing
constraints: Must not break public API signatures
Must add SAFETY comments for all @unchecked Sendable
Must complete in phased approach (4 phases)

requirements.text: Fix all Actor-Protocol Conformance issues (400 errors) - Resolve protocol conformance errors where actors need to properly handle isolated and nonisolated members
acceptance_criteria: Zero actor-protocol conformance errors reported by Swift compiler with -strict-concurrency=complete
All protocol methods on actors are marked with @MainActor, nonisolated, or actor-isolated as appropriate
Protocol conformance for streaming transcription services passes strict concurrency checks
Code compiles with Swift 6 without any Sendable conformance warnings for actor-bound protocols

requirements.text: Fix all Sendable Violations (300 errors) - Ensure all types crossing actor boundaries conform to Sendable
acceptance_criteria: Zero Sendable violations reported by Swift compiler
All types passed across actors are Sendable or use @unchecked Sendable with documented safety rationale
Transcription models and audio buffers properly conform to Sendable
All completion handlers and async closures use Sendable types
Every @unchecked Sendable has a SAFETY comment explaining thread-safety rationale

requirements.text: Fix Visibility Mismatches (150 errors) - Resolve access control and visibility conflicts in actor contexts
acceptance_criteria: Zero visibility mismatch errors reported by Swift compiler
Public/internal access modifiers are consistent across actor boundaries
Cross-module type visibility maintains ABI compatibility
All exported API signatures remain unchanged (backward compatible)

requirements.text: Fix Async-Safe Locking Issues (250 errors) - Replace unsafe locking primitives with actor-safe alternatives
acceptance_criteria: Zero async-locking errors reported by Swift compiler
All NSLock/NSRecursiveLock usage is eliminated or properly isolated
Circular buffer operations are actor-safe or use proper synchronization
Audio engine state access is properly serialized through actors
No potential for data races in concurrent audio processing paths

requirements.text: Fix Type Inference Failures (200 errors) - Resolve concurrency-related type inference issues
acceptance_criteria: Zero type inference errors in concurrent contexts reported by Swift compiler
All inferred types in async contexts are explicitly typed where required
Generic type parameters in async methods are properly constrained
Closures in async contexts have explicit type annotations
Result types in async functions are fully qualified

requirements.text: Enable Full Test Suite Compilation (OpenOatsTests target) - Ensure all tests compile with strict concurrency
acceptance_criteria: OpenOatsTests target compiles with -strict-concurrency=complete with zero errors
All test doubles and mocks are Sendable-compliant
Test expectations and async assertions are concurrency-safe
Test framework dependencies are Swift 6 compatible
swift test command executes without compilation errors

requirements.text: Document @unchecked Sendable Safety Rationales - Add SAFETY comments for all unchecked Sendable conformances
acceptance_criteria: Every @unchecked Sendable has a SAFETY: comment directly above the conformance
SAFETY comments explain why the type is thread-safe (immutable, properly locked, etc.)
Documentation is consistent with Apple Swift concurrency guidelines
All safety rationales are reviewed and approved in code review

requirements.text: Maintain Public API Compatibility - No breaking changes to public API signatures
acceptance_criteria: All public API signatures remain unchanged after Swift 6 compliance
No function signatures modified in a breaking way
No public type definitions changed incompatibly
Existing integration tests pass without modification
Semantic versioning remains compatible (minor bump only)

requirements.text: Implement Phased Migration Strategy - Execute migration in 4 phases with intermediate validation
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1 (Mocks) complete: Test doubles and mock implementations are Swift 6 compliant
Phase 2 (Protocols) complete: Protocol definitions and actor conformance resolved
Phase 3 (Actors) complete: Core actor implementations are strict concurrency compliant
Phase 4 (Tests) complete: Full test suite compiles and passes with strict concurrency
Each phase has passing intermediate build status

requirements.text: Preserve Runtime Behavior - All functional behavior remains identical pre/post migration
acceptance_criteria: All existing unit tests pass without modification
Performance benchmarks show no regression >5%
Audio processing latency remains within 20ms target
Memory usage patterns remain equivalent
Integration tests pass with identical results

requirements.text: Enable CI/CD Pipeline Integration - Configure automated strict concurrency checking in CI
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline runs swift build with -strict-concurrency=complete
Build fails on any Swift 6 concurrency errors
GitHub Actions workflow configured for Swift 6 checks
Pull request checks include strict concurrency validation
CI completes in under 10 minutes

requirements.text: Create Comprehensive Documentation - Document migration patterns and lessons learned
acceptance_criteria: Migration guide created for team reference
Common Swift 6 error patterns documented with solutions
Code examples show before/after for each error category
Architecture Decision Record (ADR) created for Swift 6 adoption
Documentation reviewed by at least 2 engineers

requirements.text: Perform Performance Validation - Measure and validate performance impact of concurrency changes
acceptance_criteria: Baseline performance metrics captured before migration
Post-migration performance metrics collected and compared
Audio buffer processing latency measured (<20ms target)
CPU usage during transcription compared pre/post
Performance regression >10% triggers investigation

requirements.text: Address Remaining 'Other' Category Errors (106 errors) - Resolve miscellaneous Swift 6 issues
acceptance_criteria: All remaining 'other' category errors categorized and resolved
Zero Swift 6 errors of any category remaining
Compiler warnings triaged (info vs fix required)

requirements.text: Implement Property-Based Testing for Concurrency - Add property-based tests for concurrent operations
acceptance_criteria: Property-based tests added for circular buffer operations
Round-trip tests for audio processing functions
Invariant tests for actor state consistency
Tests run as part of CI pipeline

risks.description: Runtime behavior regression - Actor isolation changes may alter execution timing, potentially affecting audio processing latency and synchronization
risks.mitigation: Comprehensive testing with audio latency benchmarks, A/B comparison of pre/post behavior, gradual rollout with feature flags if needed

risks.description: API compatibility break - Fixing Sendable violations may require changing public API signatures, breaking existing integrations
risks.mitigation: Use @unchecked Sendable where necessary with documented safety rationale, prefer non-breaking changes, maintain deprecated overloads during transition

risks.description: Performance degradation - Actor isolation may introduce suspension points and context switches, impacting real-time audio performance
risks.mitigation: Profile hot paths early, use nonisolated for pure computations, optimize actor hopping patterns, maintain <20ms audio buffer processing target

risks.description: Scope expansion - 1406 errors across 50 files suggests potential for hidden complexity and cascading dependencies
risks.mitigation: Strict phased approach with intermediate checkpoints, early validation of error estimates, weekly progress reviews, escalate if >20% scope increase

risks.description: Third-party dependency issues - External libraries may not be Swift 6 compliant, blocking compilation
risks.mitigation: Audit dependencies early, fork and patch if needed, seek alternative libraries, document workarounds in migration guide

risks.description: Developer productivity impact - Strict concurrency compiler errors may slow development velocity during migration
risks.mitigation: Provide clear error resolution patterns, maintain Swift 6 best practices guide, pair programming for complex cases

stakeholders.concern: Maintaining development velocity while implementing strict concurrency

stakeholders.name: Tech Lead / Architecture
stakeholders.concern: Ensuring architectural patterns are correctly applied across all actors

stakeholders.name: QA Team
stakeholders.concern: Validating that concurrency changes don't introduce regression bugs

stakeholders.name: Product Management
stakeholders.concern: Timeline impact on feature delivery schedule

stakeholders.name: macOS Users
stakeholders.concern: Application stability and audio quality post-migration

competitive_signals: Apple is pushing Swift 6 strict concurrency as the default in Xcode 16+
Other macOS audio apps are adopting Swift 6 for improved safety and performance
Swift 6 adoption is becoming table stakes for professional macOS applications
Early adopters report improved runtime stability and fewer crashes
research_signals: Swift 6 strict concurrency eliminates entire classes of data race bugs at compile time
Actor isolation provides clear ownership boundaries for mutable state
The migration pattern for audio apps is well-established in the Swift community
Property-based testing is particularly effective for validating concurrent code correctness
Most errors (~1300/1406) are in 5 categories with known fix patterns
